Theme

Latin word

quam

quam (+ superlative)

quam with a superlative adjective or adverb

as … as possible; how (to what degree); as … as possible; quam prīmum, as soon as possible; than

In this lexicon

  • as … as

    also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 6.7.3: tū tamen quam frequentissimē scrībe; Cato Agr. 66: quam mundissimē pūrissimēque fīat

  • how

    also used · classical · Traupman 330

  • possible

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.4.1: quam prīmum; Cic. Fam. 14.14.2: quam saepissimē; Traupman 54, 86; Traupman 55: quam prīmum, as soon as possible; Traupman 193: quam prīmum

  • than

    the recommended word · classical · Sen. Ep. 47.2: ēst ille plūs quam capit; Publ. R 24: Rogantī melius quam imperantī pāreās.

  • tam similis quam lacte lactī est: as like as two peas in a pod

    classical

  • tam … quam: as … as

    classical

  • potius sērō quam numquam: better late than never

    classical

  • ānsa quam manū prehendimus: handhold

    * our formation

  • nihil mihi longius est quam ut: look forward to

    classical

  • quam plūrimum: maximum

    classical

  • magis … quam: rather

    classical

  • mīrum quam (quantum): surprisingly

    classical

  • quam dūdum: when

    classical

  • quam ob rem (quamobrem): why

    classical

Examples

  • nam mellītus erat suamque nōrat ipsam tam bene quam puella mātrem

    for he was sweet as honey, and knew his mistress as well as a little girl knows her motherCatull. 3.6–7

    In the entry for as … as

    let it be done as cleanly and purely as possibleCato Agr. 66

    In the entry for as … as

    or as many as the stars, when the night is silentCatull. 7.7
